To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the regulation of ammonium metabolism in E. coli is complex, that it is robust against changes in ammonium availability, that the fluxes of GS and GDH, however, are not, and that gene expression is the key regulator of the system.

the ammonium assimilatory system is a robust system, that the system is not robust against changes in gene expression of GOGA, and that the system is nonrobust against changes in the activities of the enzymes GS and GDH.
ammonium assimilation in E. coli is a highly regulated process, and that the regulation is multifarious and subtle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the regulatory network of the ammonium‐assililating enzymes of E. coli.
the question whether the network of ammonium assimilatory enzymes is complete and sufficient to explain the regulation of ammonium uptake, ammonium assimilation, and glutamine synthesis.

the question whether the regulation of the ammonium‐assimating enzymes GS and GDH of Escherichiacoli is sufficient to ensure robustness of ammonium assimilating flux, and whether this is achieved by a network that is sufficiently complete to explain all of the observed behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ammonium assimilation in E. coli is regulated by multiple mechanisms and that the regulation is multifarious.
the ammonium assimilating enzymes of E. coli are regulated by a complex network, which leads to subtle and non‐obvious regulation of the fluxes through the enzymes.
GS and GDH, and the network that regulates them, are not only important for the assimilation of ammonium, but also for the survival of E. coli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although we are still far from a complete understanding of the regulatory network of ammonium assimilating enzymes, the model we developed is a good approximation of the real network.
ammonium assimilation in E. coli is regulated by a complex network of interactions between the components of the ammonium‐assimating pathway, which leads to a quasi‐intelligent response.
we have shown that the ammonium assimilating system of E. coli is a highly sophisticated regulatory system that is capable of adapting to a variety of environmental conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the network that regulates ammonium assimilation in E. coli is a highly sophisticated system, in which the individual regulators interact in a complex way, and that the network is able to respond in a highly specific way to changes in the ammonum and carbon status of a cell.
the ammonium assimilatory pathway of E. coli is regulated in a multifarious manner.
the regulation of ammonium metabolism is multifaceted and subtle.
